summary: Give loop round gate agents durable mission-path/rN/gate identities

replay.detail: New round mission-run.created claims record the canonical gate agent. Creation replay preserves hash-named selectors when this field is absent, so pre-upgrade claimed work keeps its completion authority. Existing round selectors are cut over only by durable step-run.state claims after work drains and the legacy runtime stops. No full projection rebuild is requested by the change.

schema.detail: The mission-run.created claim contract gains an optional gate_agent reference for canonical round identity. The step-run.state contract gains optional gate_agent and previous_gate_agent references for replayable assignment cutover. No database table/index/trigger or numeric database schema version changes.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rules version or retention classification change; step-run.state was already durable. Upgrade mission-owning daemons together as described under compatibility, not as a checkpoint-rules transition.

compatibility.detail: Durable round gate subjects and display names change from agent/<run hash>/gate to agent/<mission path>/r<N>/gate. Root mission and builder identities and run-derived runtime IDs remain unchanged. ST_GATE_AGENT supplies the full canonical gate subject. Older daemons do not implement the new assignment cutover; mixed-version writers and downgrade after migration are not supported. Upgrade all daemons that can own these rounds before starting new gate work.

downtime.detail: Claimed legacy gate work keeps its completion authority and drains before gate retirement. A round waits for positive legacy-runtime absence before the new gate can start, so cutover interruption depends on work and runtime shutdown. Restart-to-API and restart-to-health were not measured.

manual.detail: Upgrade the mission-owning daemons to this source. Existing work migrates automatically at a safe gate boundary. Inspect any occupied mission/round gate identity and complete or cancel its owning run; competing live ownership is rejected instead of overwritten. Use agent/<mission path>/r<N>/gate in new operator references, and confirm assignments and owner run agree before restarting a gate.

recovery.detail: Roll forward if a cutover is waiting or faulted. Retained hash-named claimed work remains valid until drained. Binary rollback does not reverse durable assignment cutover or restore hash gate identities; do not run an older mission owner against migrated rounds. Resolve conflicting ownership or missing-runtime faults through the normal run and agent controls, then continue on the new build.
